findings.title: #382 persists, but this head fails earlier than the archived output
findings.detail:
Executed the requested int_column_name.py probe under pandas 3.0.1, 2.3.3 and 2.0.0. Each printed 'fit + predict: ok', then stopped at line 51 because tempfile.mkdtemp() found no writable directory. lizyml.__file__ pointed into this workspace in every environment. The tree lacks build-generated _version.py, so probes supplied only that module in memory.
To exercise the remaining paths without repository edits, a second harness redirected filesystem operations to memory, retained actual JSON/joblib serialization and checksum validation, and redirected LightGBM model-file writes to model_to_string(). Public export_code succeeded for the integer categorical case, but the generated predictor raised 'pipeline_state.json has a malformed identity_columns'. Categories have JSON key '7', while identity_columns contains integer 7. Removing the identity marker from the serialized state reproduced the archived failure: 'could not convert string to float'. The underlying name-loss diagnosis is correct; the observed exception in the issue description needs updating for this head.

findings.title: The accepted population includes working non-string numeric projects
findings.detail:
Executed a 75-case matrix on pandas 3.0.1: 25 label types, each on numeric, object categorical and declared-category columns, alongside string-named x and target columns. Models used 120 rows, two folds and three boosting rounds. Results below distinguish fit failures from serialization failures; they do not propose changing LightGBM.
Fit, runtime predict and memory-backed Model.export → Model.load → predict worked for all three column kinds named str, numpy.str_ or Python int. Python float, Python bool and every other tested NumPy scalar worked as numeric column names only. The additional NumPy names tested were int8/16/32/64, uint8/16/32/64, float16/32/64, longdouble, bool_, bytes_, complex64/128, datetime64 and timedelta64. All 29 fitted cases preserved predictions through persistence, with maximum absolute difference 0.
Categorical float and NumPy names other than str_ failed during fit, generally with 'Wrong type ... in categorical_feature'; bool/bool_ categorical names raised a pandas wrong-length ValueError, and float16 categorical names raised NotImplementedError. None failed for all three kinds on pandas 3.0.1 with KeyError '[nan] not in index'. Tuple ('a','b') failed for all kinds; a genuine MultiIndex frame also failed. Three separate mixed 7/'7' collision cases failed during fit because the estimator received duplicate textual feature names.
Of the 29 fitted cases, current export_code produced 12 projects: six string-name cases, three integer-name cases, and numeric float, bool and float64 cases. Generated predict worked in 10; the two integer categorical cases failed identity validation. Generated train retrained all 12 with writes redirected to memory, but its newly written integer categorical states failed prediction again. The other 17 fitted cases failed export_code with raw JSON TypeError for their NumPy label.
The original 33-case subset was repeated under pandas 2.3.3 and 2.0.0. Its results matched except numeric None also worked through fit, persistence, generated prediction and retraining. Thus a blanket string-only rule would remove working behavior.

findings.title: Configured column roles already have a different naming contract
findings.detail:
Executed constructor validation for target, time_col, group_col, features.exclude and features.categorical across the tested labels. Numeric, bool, tuple and NumPy numeric/temporal names were refused with CONFIG_INVALID. None was refused for target and list entries; for time_col/group_col it means the role is disabled, not that a None-named column is selected. numpy.str_ was accepted and converted to str. numpy.bytes_ was also accepted but decoded to text: b'c' became 'c', which refers to a string label rather than the bytes label.
For actual string and numpy.str_ role names, separate fits covering target, time-series splitting, group splitting, exclusion and explicit categoricals passed runtime prediction, memory-backed export/load, export_code and generated retraining. Setting a required role to '7' when the actual label was integer 7 raised DATA_SCHEMA_INVALID. Setting exclude=['7'] or categorical=['7'] did not select integer 7; the fit retained that feature. dataframe_builder.py:68-79 and :116-118 perform these lookups without coercion.
The Proposal must distinguish feature labels discovered from a frame from names supplied through configuration. Expanding configured role types would be an additional contract change, not a necessary consequence of fixing #382.

findings.title: Persistence preserves prediction identity but already loses declared-category keys
findings.detail:
The name-bearing paths differ. Runtime pipeline state stores feature_names/categorical_cols as lists and encoder categories/modes as dictionaries; identity_columns and stand_in_columns are name lists. FitResult also holds a dtype dictionary keyed by labels. Joblib preserves these objects. LightGBM text stores textual feature names; generated prediction supplies an array in recorded feature order (templates.py:1762-1767).
config_writer.py:111-134 writes feature_names and categorical_features as JSON values but declared_categories as an object keyed by labels. artifact_writer.py:35-55 does the same for pipeline categories and writes identity names as values. persistence metadata writes feature_names with default=str and declared_categories as object keys. Neither loader.py:426-429 nor _model_persistence.py:137-143 restores those key types.
Executed export/load of a declared categorical feature named 7 preserved prediction exactly, but loaded declared_categories had key '7'. Therefore 'Model.export works' is true for measured prediction round trips, not exact preservation of all metadata. The existing category preflight does not detect this: _category_preflight.py:72-75 round-trips category values while retaining the original column keys. Adding a Model.export refusal would remove 23 working persistence cases in the 75-case matrix; it should not be bundled into an export_code fix without an explicit decision.

findings.title: Typed artifact names alone cannot define the generated file-input contract
findings.detail:
Both generated entry points directly call read_csv/read_parquet; predict has the corresponding path at templates.py:1800. Executed CSV round trips changed integer 7 to header '7', float 7.5 to '7.5' and bool True to 'True'. None produced 'Unnamed: 0'. Current numeric non-string projects that predict correctly on typed frames consequently fail on CSV. Only the six string-name cases passed ordinary CSV prediction in the primary matrix.
Executed BytesIO parquet round trips in all three environments also stringified ordinary numeric labels in these mixed-column frames. numpy.bytes_(b'c') became string 'c'. None survived as None under pandas 2.3.3/2.0.0 but returned as NaN under pandas 3.0.1. Parquet therefore cannot be assumed to preserve arbitrary label identity.
For option (a), CSV must use an explicit, validated header-to-label mapping or fail clearly; decoding JSON names does not decode CSV headers. For string-only options (b)/(c), existing string-schema CSV behavior remains. For fit normalization (d), input files must be written using the normalized schema. The recommended project-alias alternative likewise needs published canonical headers: raw None-header CSV and bytes-label parquet require explicit renaming, not guessing from parser-generated headers.

findings.title: Options have materially different compatibility costs
findings.detail:
Counts below use the 75-case pandas 3.0.1 matrix: 69 cases have non-string labels, 29 fit, 23 fitted cases have non-string labels, and 10 currently predict successfully in generated code. Counts for proposed guards are evaluated against observed schemas; prototype results are identified separately.
(a) Preserve typed names: use a versioned name table and positions for categories, declared categories and identity columns. Touch config_writer.py:111-143, artifact_writer.py:31-55, template config/state readers, train's state writer at templates.py:386-405, and identity validation so decoding occurs before membership checks. Runtime fit need not change. Exact metadata preservation additionally touches persistence exporter/loader and _checked_declared_categories. A primary-subset transport prototype preserved all 15 fitted cases and repaired five failures: two integer categoricals and three NumPy JSON failures. Supporting the additional 14 fitted NumPy cases requires a defined name codec; that implementation was not measured. H-0133 is insufficient unchanged: executed encode/decode converts NumPy scalar names to Python scalars and refuses None. Existing standalone projects require regeneration; new readers need an explicit legacy-format branch.
(b) Refuse non-string names at export_code: add a shared preflight at the facade and direct generator boundary before writes, raising SERIALIZATION_FAILED. No runtime, template, identity_template or persistence-format change is required. With isinstance(name,str), this affects 23 fitted matrix cases: six currently successful exports become refusals, 17 raw JSON failures become named refusals, and four currently working numeric predictors plus six successful retraining paths are lost. Applying it to Model.export additionally removes all 23 working non-string persistence round trips. Existing standalone projects remain unchanged and broken projects remain broken.
(c) Refuse at fit: validate effective feature labels around model.py:813, after role/exclusion selection. It changes admission/error behavior in 69/75 cases and removes 23 working fits. A fit-only guard does not cover already-saved models loaded and exported later; export_code still needs a guard. Existing artifacts should remain loadable. Templates and identity_template need no new name representation.
(d) Normalize at fit: change data preparation and define prediction identity, dtype/category dictionaries and saved-schema semantics consistently. Executed rename(columns=str) prototypes increased successful fits from 29 to 72/75; the three tuple cases still failed. All 23 previously working typed-label cases then rejected their original typed prediction frames and accepted normalized frames. This is a substantial runtime contract change. Old artifacts must retain old lookup semantics rather than being silently normalized on load; generated code can use its current string representation once every name-bearing field is consistent.

findings.title: Recommend project-only string aliases with an explicit acceptance contract
findings.detail:
Recommend an additional option (e): retain runtime and saved-model identities, but define generated projects to use unique string aliases for columns. Apply aliases consistently to config, categories, declared categories, identity columns and every generated input boundary. This addresses file headers without changing fit/predict identity or adding a typed-name persistence format.
Executed an in-memory prototype using str(label) aliases on copied export state and input adapters around the actual rendered scripts. All 29 fitted matrix cases exported, predicted from typed frames and ordinary CSV, retrained, and predicted afterward with maximum absolute difference 0. It repaired all 19 generated-prediction failures and preserved the 10 working predictors. It changed project schemas for 23 cases and expanded successful CSV prediction from six to 29. Under both older pandas environments, numeric None also worked with typed frames and canonical 'None'-header CSV; raw blank-header CSV correctly failed. This is prototype evidence, not a completed implementation.
The code sites are generator/config/artifact name handling and generated train/predict entry points; test_equivalence input handling must use the same policy. identity_template.py can retain its membership logic because both sides become strings. Runtime and persistence writers/loaders need no format change for this option. Use an explicit project policy marker so legacy projects retain their interpretation. Already-exported standalone scripts require regeneration; existing saved models remain loadable and can be re-exported.
A closed Proposal acceptance list should require: (1) string and numpy.str_ controls; Python int/finite float/bool; the enumerated NumPy integer, floating, bool, bytes, complex and temporal scalar names; and numeric None where fit already supports it. Tuple/MultiIndex fit support is not expanded. Other name types must receive a named export refusal until admitted explicitly. (2) Numeric, auto categorical and declared categorical features; mixed labels; string target/time/group/exclusion roles; original and loaded models; direct generator entry; generated predict, train, retrain-then-predict and equivalence paths. (3) Canonical CSV/parquet headers, typed in-memory inputs, and explicit failures for ambiguous aliases or parser-mangled headers. Reject duplicate aliases before dictionaries or column selection can merge them. (4) Public export errors use SERIALIZATION_FAILED with surface='export_code', a stable reason such as column_name_collision/unsupported_column_name, and offending positions, qualified types, reprs and aliases; validate before any write. Generated schema errors should remain ValueError-compatible and carry an equally explicit reason and offending names. (5) Preserve legacy saved-model lookup and category-value behavior. The owner must approve this project-specific identity contract; its acceptance of textual aliases is intentional.

findings.title: Measured suite exposure is zero in the reached population, with an incomplete full-suite denominator
findings.detail:
Executed an in-memory pytest census plugin over tests with cache, bytecode and fd capture disabled. It intercepted Model.fit, resolved explicit or constructor-held DataFrames, removed configured target/time/group/excluded columns, counted labels with not isinstance(label,str), and stopped each reached test at fit before training. Result: 0/4,300 non-string feature columns across 1,836 reached fit calls; raw input labels also contained no non-strings. One call had unresolved data. The command was an instrumented census, not a passing regression run.
This is not a complete count of successful suite fits: stopping at the first fit hides later fits in a test, tuning/adapter training was skipped, and file-dependent setup remained blocked in the read-only environment. A full-suite n/N could not be measured here. tests/test_tuning/test_objective_identity.py:73 does construct an integer-label variant for identity checks, so absence from this census does not imply absence from all test data.
All naming policies have zero column firings in this observed suite population. For the measured probe matrix, (b) affects 23 reachable export cases, (c) changes 69 fit admissions/errors, (d) changes 69 feature identities, and recommended (e) changes 23 project schemas while repairing 19 prediction failures. Option (a)'s executed primary prototype repairs five cases; its broader codec remains a design dependency.
